findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key credentials are embedded in EC2 user data, placing them in Terraform source/state and making them readable through instance/user-data access paths. An attacker obtaining these credentials can authenticate as the associated IAM principal until the key is revoked or rotated.

No metadata_options configuration requires IMDSv2, so the instance can permit IMDSv1. A server-side request forgery vulnerability on the host could retrieve instance metadata and any role credentials exposed through it.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (and no customer-managed KMS key), so its data can be created unencrypted unless an external account-level default happens to enforce encryption.

This snapshot is created from the unencrypted EBS volume and has no encryption configuration; EBS snapshots inherit the source volume's encryption state. It therefore stores a copy of the volume's data without encryption at rest.

TCP port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing any internet host to reach the instance's SSH service. This exposes the host to scanning, brute-force attacks, and exploitation of SSH or host authentication weaknesses.
The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 for egress. This provides an unrestricted path for data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised instance.
The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Flow-log objects may therefore be stored without explicitly enforced encryption at rest.
